back: Attraction between a δ+ H atom bonded to N, O or F and a lone pair on an N, O or F atom of another molecule.

front: How do instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces arise?
back: Moving electrons create a temporary dipole in one molecule, which induces a dipole in a neighbour; the two attract.

front: What increases instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces?
back: More electrons (larger Mr) and greater surface contact (unbranched chains).
The general name for instantaneous dipole-induced dipole and permanent dipole-permanent dipole forces.

front: Why is ice less dense than water?
back: Each molecule forms four hydrogen bonds in an open tetrahedral lattice, holding molecules further apart than in the liquid.
High melting and boiling points, high surface tension, ice less dense than liquid water: all due to hydrogen bonding.

front: What is overcome when a simple molecular substance boils?
back: Only the intermolecular forces; covalent bonds within molecules are unchanged.

front: Effect of branching on alkane boiling points?
back: More branching → less surface contact → weaker instantaneous dipole forces → lower boiling point.

front: What happens to a jet of water near a charged rod?
back: It bends towards the rod (either charge): polar molecules align their opposite end to the rod.
